result.keywords: This article examines how nineteenth-century anthologies of coastal verse employed marble-like imagery to frame memory, tide, and civic ritual. It combines archival reading with comparative poetics to analyze recurring motifs of lanterns, harbors, salt weathering, and funerary light across small-press collections. The study argues that marble serves less as a material reference than as a symbolic device for permanence, loss, and public commemoration in maritime lyric traditions.
result.title: Marble Lanterns in Coastal Poetry Anthologies.
